stops.note: the Andean name, an imitation of its squeak; the Inca kept cuy for food, as many Andean families still do
Spanish colonists adopted the Quechua word and also called it 'conejillo de Indias', little rabbit of the Indies
neither from Guinea nor a pig: its name may come from Guiana or the slave-trade route via Guinea; 'guinea pig', a test subject, dates from the 1920s

current_meaning: a small South American rodent kept as a pet or used in experiments
